sources.entry: LibrePhotos - Photo management service with a slight focus on cool graphs (alternative to Google Photos). (Clients) MIT Python/Docker
LibrePhotos | Photo management with face recognition and AI-powered search

summary.one_liner: LibrePhotos is a self-hosted, open-source photo management service with face recognition, object detection, and semantic search.
summary.what_it_does: It is a monorepo containing a Django/Django REST Framework backend with ML pipelines and background jobs, a React 19 and Vite web frontend, an Expo mobile app for Android and iOS, a Docusaurus docs site, and deployment configs (Dockerfiles, Compose, Nginx proxy, Kubernetes manifests). It scans existing folders and accepts uploads, handling RAW, HEIC, JPEG XL, videos and live photos. Face detection and clustering let you name a person once and have the rest suggested. Machine learning features generate tags, captions, and semantic search such as "dog on a beach", and find similar photos. Other features include timeline and map views from reverse geocoding, event-based albums, multiple users with shared albums and public links, duplicate detection, and OpenID Connect single sign-on.
use_cases: automatic face recognition in a personal photo library
semantic search of photos by content
organizing RAW and HEIC photos on a home server
sharing albums and public photo links with family
backing up phone photos from an Android or iOS app
how_to_run: Choose a deployment: single container, Docker Compose, Kubernetes (deploy/k8s), Unraid, or Windows standalone (librephotos.exe)
Single container: one image serves the API and web app (recommended for most people)
Docker Compose: separate backend, frontend and proxy containers, optional NVIDIA GPU acceleration
Follow the step-by-step installation guides in the documentation
After starting, open the Swagger UI or ReDoc API docs at the URLs given in the README
notable: Machine learning runs on ONNX Runtime with no PyTorch dependency
Monorepo consolidating five previously separate repositories, with history preserved
Face clustering and captioning use recognised people and places as context
Windows standalone build needs no Docker or Python
Includes an Expo mobile app with offline-first design
caveats: Machine learning features are memory-intensive; 8 GB+ RAM is strongly recommended
Minimum system requirements are 4 GB RAM and 2 cores
Setup details are deferred to external documentation
